artifact_version_note: artifact_version is derived here: it names the per-level gate-produced versions together, because each level is gated and scored as its own task instance. The gate's own values are in `levels`.

artifact.definition: does the station's daily maximum observed water level exceed its published NOS minor flood threshold on the target day
artifact.source: the ten artifact files fetched from private staging by the job itself and measured in place: these are the bytes being released, not a rebuild

calibration.method: single stock features and a plain 'yesterday exceeded' rule, no training; rank-based AUC; the eval split only
calibration.question: how much of the baseline's AUC is persistence rather than prediction

baseline.calibration_note: the persistence floor was measured with code/persistence_baseline.py against the noaa-003 eval split (staging release 392230750). The corrected artifact has identical rows and positives in every split, but a few observation values were revised between the two pulls, so those single-feature figures are carried over as measured on those bytes rather than re-measured on the released ones
baseline.dependencies: recorded in this job's container.log: pandas 2.3.3, numpy 2.5.3, xgboost 3.4.1, scikit-learn 1.9.1 (installed from the runner's declared ranges). noaa-baseline-001 did not record its versions; this rerun closes that gap for the recorded figure

previous_measurement.why: measured on the superseded artifact, whose only schema difference is the label column name (`late`), copied from the Austin task. Rows and positives are identical in all six splits; the third decimal differs because xgboost's training is not bit-reproducible, so the two measurements agree to about 0.0005

baseline.purpose: one baseline through the runner's existing training and validation contract, on both levels of the artifact the release will carry

runner_files.note: the benchmark's own train.py, validate.py and validate.sh, copied verbatim; validate.py re-ran training and reported CONTRACT OK on both levels

baseline.scope: one baseline only. No coding agent and no harness comparison was run, and none is implied.

data_compilation.scope: Our contribution: the frozen station list, the row selection, the derived binary label, the temporal and station-disjoint partitions, the feature construction and the packaging. Does not cover or relicense NOAA's data.

rules: Code and documentation: MIT by default.
Our rights in a derived compilation: CC0-1.0 by default.
The source's own terms are preserved and never relicensed; the compilation dedication covers only our contribution.

Each dataset must use terms compatible with its sources. CC0 is NOT a blanket override of upstream terms: attribution, share-alike and non-commercial requirements from a source are carried through unchanged.
A source whose licence terms cannot be read is not published at all.
The chosen terms are declared per dataset in candidates/<id>/license.json and recorded in the release manifest, so the manifest cannot drift from the decision.

source_data.attribution: NOAA National Ocean Service, Center for Operational Oceanographic Products and Services (CO-OPS), verified water level observations and flood thresholds, https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/, accessed 2026-09-18
source_data.citation: NOAA CO-OPS. Verified daily maximum water level observations (product daily_max_min) and minor flood thresholds (station metadata API) for 122 NOS stations, 2006-2025. Retrieved 2026-09-18 from https://api.tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/. Public Domain. Derived dataset: NOAA tide flooding prediction dataset, version 2026.09.
source_data.derived_labelling: Labelled as derived throughout; not an official NOAA, NOS or NWS product. The source's own constraint - modified content must not be presented as official government material - is honoured.
evidence: READ 2026-09-19 from the CO-OPS portal itself (the same host the data comes from), https://tidesandcurrents.noaa.gov/disclaimers.html, 'Use of Data and Products': "The information on government servers are in the public domain, unless specifically annotated otherwise, and may be used freely by the public." Same page: "NOS requests that attribution be given whenever NOS material is reproduced and re-disseminated. Pursuant to 17 U.S.C. 403 ... stating that such material is not subject to copyright protection." CONSTRAINT READ ON THE SAME PAGE, honoured in the release: "This information shall not be modified in content and then presented as official government material" - any derived dataset must be labelled as derived and must not be presented as official NOS data. Corroborating: nauticalcharts.noaa.gov/data/data-licensing.html records NOAA data released under a CC0-1.0 public-domain dedication (CC BY 4.0 for some products), and the NCEI ISO metadata for CO-OPS stations carries the same CC0 waiver. Attributes: attribution requested as a courtesy, not required.

coverage.note: Coverage is a hard condition, not an observation: the builder exits non-zero on a single lost station-year, so an incomplete panel cannot be scored as the frozen one.

cases.name: bomb-cyclone record tide
cases.why: Boston's documented record tide. Any datum handling that denies flooding here is wrong.

cases.name: 2025 annual maximum
cases.why: The highest tide of the station-year used for the base-rate measurement.

external_validation.claim: NOAA's authoritative annual product reports minCount 2 for 2025, matching the STND reconstruction (2 exceeding days) and contradicting the MLLW one (0).

measured.purpose: Regression fixture for NOAA CO-OPS datum handling. Recorded so a future change cannot silently reintroduce the MLLW-vs-threshold bug, which produced zero positives at every station.
measured.rule: Compare observed water levels to the published NOS flood thresholds using datum=STND. The MDAPI floodlevels response carries no datum field, and datum=MLLW makes the comparison silently fail.

datum.requirement: MUST use datum=STND. The published nos_minor threshold is in the station datum and the metadata API does not declare a datum. Comparing MLLW-referenced heights to nos_minor silently yields zero positives at every station; see measurements.datum_trap_measured.

extraction_cost.note: The route matters: the raw 6-minute series would have been 29,160 requests and about 15.2 GiB. One request per station-year per product is 4,880 requests and about 184 MB, and it is the publisher's own verified product.
extraction_cost.route: daily_max_min features + HTF daily flags, one request each per station-year

label_route.correction: our reduction of 6-minute maxima overcounted flood days by ~20% against NOAA's own counts on 2024 (113-114 vs 94 over four stations); NOAA's own flags matched exactly, station by station
label_route.note: A label that disagrees with the publisher's own product has to be justified, and there is no reason to ship one. Our own reduction overcounted by about 20%.
label_route.source: NOAA HTF daily product, field minFlag (the publisher's own minor-flood days)

persistence_calibration.accuracy_trap: the plain rule 'yesterday exceeded the threshold' agrees with the label about 96% of the time while scoring 0.63 AUC, because only ~2% of days are positive. Accuracy would flatter a useless rule, which is why the contract scores AUC.
persistence_calibration.command: python3 code/persistence_baseline.py --fetch (eval split only; no training)
persistence_calibration.why: the honest floor: what a single stock feature achieves with no learning at all

threshold_decision.decision: the published physical nos_minor threshold is retained
threshold_decision.why: it is the quantity coastal flood statements are actually issued against; it is not replaced with a per-station quantile chosen to balance the classes

publication_note: Prepared for human review. Nothing here has been published.

qualification.note: Two earlier runs failed on coverage, not on the data: noaa-001 lost 13 stations and noaa-002 lost 60 station-years to fetch errors the retry treated as permanent. Both were fixed in the builder, which now records coverage and refuses an incomplete panel.
